citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
A review of records for protocol 061620-1-2026 revealed a significant deviation from the approved IACUC study protocol.
On June 17, 2026, out of three pigs, all were given more xylazine and less telazol than detailed in the protocol and two
were given more heparin than detailed in the protocol. On July 22, 2026, out of seven pigs, all were given more xylazine
and less telazol than detailed in the protocol and four were given more heparin than detailed in the protocol. The study
protocol states xylazine should be given at 1-2 mg/kg, telazol at 3-5 mg/kg, and heparin at 100-500 IU/kg. On average,
ten animals received 2.4 mg/kg of xylazine, ten animals received 2.4 mg/kg of telazol, and six animals received 519
mg/kg of heparin.
This activity constitutes a significant deviation from the approved activities in the protocol. Making significant changes to
protocols without IACUC review and approval deprives the IACUC of the opportunity to provide oversight of animal
activities and compliance with the Animal Welfare Act. Failing to complete assessments as described in the IACUC
protocol could result in unrecognized suffering in the affected animals.
Principal investigators are to follow the IACUC approved protocols, and any proposed changes shall be reviewed and
approved by the IACUC prior to implementation. Those carrying out procedures in an IACUC-approved protocol must
adhere to what was approved by the IACUC.
Correct by August 6, 2026.

citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC)
citations.narrative:
The committee is not approving proposed activities involving animals at a convened IACUC meeting when approving
proposals via full committee review. Proposed animal use activities are emailed to all members of the IACUC committee
and members respond, sometimes only to the IACUC Chair, with suggested changes, approvals, or denials of the
protocols. Because of this, recommended changes for protocol 061620-1-2026 were not seen by two out of the five other
committee members, including the attending veterinarian. The suggested changes were made to this protocol and
notification of approval was sent to the principal investigators without the two committee members aware of the changes.
Convened IACUC meetings facilitate thorough committee review and deliberation of the proposed activities involving
animals, which is essential to ensure the quality of the proposed scientific work and the humane use of animals.
The research facility needs to review and approve proposed activities that involve the care and use of animals at either a
convened meeting of a quorum of IACUC members or via the designated member review process.
Correct by August 6, 2026.

citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
IACUC approved study 061620-1-2026 does not contain a rationale for the numbers of animals requested for the study,
aside from stating that the number requested is needed for “research and development purposes.”
Including a rationale for the number of animals to be used allows the IACUC to conduct a thorough review of the use of
animals in a research study. Failure to require this information can result in inappropriate use of animals in research and
unsatisfactory scientific outcomes.
The IACUC must ensure that a proposal to conduct an activity involving animals contains all required information
including a rationale for involving animals, and for the appropriateness of the species and numbers of animals to be used.
Correct by October 19, 2026.

citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
IACUC approved protocol 040420-1-26 does not contain a complete written description of the proposed use of animals.
The protocols state that heparin may be administered intra-arterially to unsedated pigs prior to collection of certain tissues
under anesthesia. The routes of administration are not specified in the protocol. The IACUC members present at the time
of the inspection were not aware which arteries were to be used for the heparin injections. The facility followed up with the
information that the jugular vein may be injected.
The IACUC is responsible for reviewing all aspects of animal care and use, and for evaluating protocols to ensure
compliance with the Animal Welfare Act. In order to properly accomplish this function, the IACUC must be aware of all
procedures being conducted. Procedures must be described completely to enable the IACUC to conduct a thorough
review of the components of the activities related to the care and use of animals, including route of administration, to
determine if the likelihood of pain or discomfort exists and to consider if/how pain and discomfort might be limited to that
which is unavoidable for the conduct of scientifically valuable research.
The IACUC must ensure that all proposals to conduct activities involving animals contain a complete description of the
proposed use of the animals, including the names, dosages, and routes of medications.
Correct by October 19, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
